test_policy.notes: CUNY-wide: test optional for undergraduate admission; first-year applicants may choose whether to submit SAT or ACT scores and the absence of scores cannot be used to deny admission. CCNY's review looks at 'SAT or ACT scores (if submitted)'. College Navigator quotes the policy as in force through the spring 2027 semester; neither CUNY nor CCNY gives an end date, so fall 2027 entry is not separately confirmed.

requirements.supplemental_essays: None required; CCNY says supporting materials are optional. Selective programs (architecture, engineering and computer science, music, premedical studies, advertising and public relations, electronic design and multimedia, sonic arts, Sophie Davis / CUNY School of Medicine) have extra requirements on their own pages.
requirements.notes: Apply with the CUNY application (not the Common App); one application can list up to 6 CUNY colleges; freshman fee $65, non-refundable (the CDS also gives $65). CUNY application fee waivers are for New York State applicants only. Send all required materials directly to CUNY, not to CCNY. CCNY reviews overall GPA, performance in core subjects (math, English, science) and SAT or ACT scores if submitted, in light of the intended major. International students are those who completed any part of secondary or post-secondary education outside the U.S. and/or need an F-1 visa; they send official certificates, detailed transcripts and certified translations, plus TOEFL, IELTS, PTE or Duolingo if their native language is not English and they hold a temporary visa. CUNY's deadline table lists February 1 for the Grove School of Engineering and the Spitzer School of Architecture (architecture needs a supplemental application) and December 1 for the Sophie Davis BS/MD program, and does not say how those dates apply to international applicants, so confirm with CCNY admissions. Housing: the CDS describes The Towers as a co-ed residence hall.

deadlines.label: International first-year application deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: CUNY lists December 1 as the application deadline for freshman applicants requesting a student visa or with full or partial credentials from outside the U.S. (U.S.-educated applicants: February 1 priority); admission is rolling from January to July. CCNY's freshman page points to CUNY for deadlines. The CUNY page prints no year for these rows; the same page shows the September 15-November 16, 2026 free-application period and Macaulay dates in 2026, so fall 2027 is assumed. Selective programs may have other dates (see requirements notes).

deadlines.label: International supporting documents due (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Transcripts and other supporting documents for international applicants, sent to CUNY (same CUNY table; no year printed).

english_policy.waiver_notes: Applicants whose native language is not English and who hold a temporary visa must submit TOEFL, IELTS (Academic), PTE (Academic) or Duolingo scores; CCNY's international page names TOEFL and IELTS, and CUNY's chart adds PTE and Duolingo. The undergraduate pages list no test exemptions. Scores are official when the testing agency sends them to CUNY or the CUNY code 2950 is listed when registering.

english.notes: Internet-based TOEFL, old 0-120 scale, from the CUNY comparison chart row for The City College of New York. The chart does not give a new 1-6 scale minimum.

aid.notes: Common Data Set H6 ticks only that institutional non-need-based scholarship and grant aid is available to degree-seeking nonresidents; institutional need-based aid is not ticked, and the number of recipients and the average award are left blank. CCNY's admissions scholarships page lists named general and specialized-high-school scholarships without stating whether international first-years are eligible. U.S. federal and New York State aid does not apply to F-1 students. F-1/J-1 students pay the nonresident tuition rate (CDS 2026-27: $18,600 for the year; CUNY 2026-27 page: $620 per credit).

sat.note: No SAT code is printed on the CUNY or CCNY pages checked; pick the college by name in the College Board search.

act.note: No ACT code is printed on the CUNY or CCNY pages checked; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: CUNY-wide university code for official test score reports (CUNY How to Apply page).

ielts.note: No IELTS institution code is listed; the page says to have the testing agency send scores to CUNY.

duolingo.note: No Duolingo institution code is listed.

pte.note: No PTE institution code is listed.

tier_notes.general: Our estimate: 58% of fall 2025 applicants admitted, SAT middle 50% of 540-700 ERW and 530-730 Math for the 11% of first-years who submitted scores (College Navigator, fall 2024), CUNY test-optional; placed with other large urban public commuter universities (Temple, Rutgers-Newark) at D+.
tier_notes.engineering: Our estimate, no ranking source checked: the Grove School of Engineering is CCNY's flagship (College Navigator shows 204 bachelor's engineering completions), so it is placed above the general tier.
tier_notes.pre_med: Our estimate, no ranking source checked: CCNY runs the Sophie Davis Biomedical Education / CUNY School of Medicine BS/MD pathway and a premedical studies program, listed among its selective programs.
tier_notes.arts_design: Our estimate, no ranking source checked: the Spitzer School of Architecture (63 bachelor's completions) and a large visual and performing arts program (171) are among CCNY's selective programs.
tier_notes.nursing: No nursing program (no bachelor's health professions completions in College Navigator).
